bottom_line: In IDEAL, high-dose atorvastatin (80 mg/d) vs usual-dose simvastatin (20 mg/d) did not significantly reduce major coronary events (HR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.78-1.01; P=.07).
implications: These data show that, compared with simvastatin 20 mg/d, atorvastatin 80 mg/d did not achieve a statistically significant reduction in the prespecified primary outcome (HR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.78-1.01; P=.07), while several secondary outcomes (eg, nonfatal myocardial infarction and major cardiovascular events) were reduced with hazard ratios below 1 and P=.02; all-cause mortality was similar (HR, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.85-1.13; P=.81).

major_points.text: Prospective, randomized, open-label trial with blinded end-point evaluation (PROBE design) conducted at 190 centers in northern Europe with median follow-up 4.8 years.
major_points.quote: The IDEAL study, a prospective, randomized, open-label, blinded end-point evaluation trial conducted at 190 ambulatory cardiology care and specialist practices in northern Europe between March 1999 and March 2005 with a median follow-up of 4.8 years

major_points.text: Patients aged 80 years or younger with prior definite myocardial infarction were randomized (n=8888).
major_points.quote: which enrolled 8888 patients aged 80 years or younger with a history of acute MI.

major_points.text: Interventions were atorvastatin 80 mg/d vs simvastatin 20 mg/d.
major_points.quote: Patients were randomly assigned to receive a high dose of atorvastatin (80 mg/d; n=4439), or usual-dose simvastatin (20 mg/d; n=4449).

major_points.text: Primary endpoint was time to first major coronary event (coronary death, nonfatal acute MI, or cardiac arrest with resuscitation).
major_points.quote: The primary clinical outcome was time to first occurrence of a major coronary event, defined as coronary death, hospitalization for nonfatal acute myocardial infarction, or cardiac arrest with resuscitation.

analysis_methods.text: All analyses were intention-to-treat including all randomized patients.
analysis_methods.quote: All analyses in this report are based on the intention- to-treat principle including all random- ized patients.

analysis_methods.text: Kaplan-Meier hazard rates and log-rank test were used; Cox proportional hazards models used to calculate HRs and 95% CIs.
analysis_methods.quote: Kaplan-Meier hazard rates were used to examine incidence over time and the log-rank test was used to assess group differences. Cox proportional hazards models were used to calculate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence in- tervals (CIs).

analysis_methods.text: Designed for 90% power to detect 21% relative risk reduction (from 10% to 7.9%) with 2-tailed alpha .05.
analysis_methods.quote: The trial was designed to have 90% power to detect an anticipated 21% relative risk reduction (from 10% to 7.9%) in the primary outcome variable with atorvastatin over 5 years using a 2-tailed ␣ level of .05.

analysis_methods.text: Planned sample size increased from 7700 to 8888 due to lower recalculated risk in early recruits.
analysis_methods.quote: the originally planned sample size of 7700 patients was increased to 8888.

analysis_methods.text: Data and safety monitoring board performed interim analyses at approximately 50% and 75% of predetermined final number of 774 primary endpoints.
analysis_methods.quote: A data and safety monitoring board per- formed interim analyses when approxi- mately 50% and 75% of the predeter- mined final number of 774 patients had experienced a primary end point.

criticisms.text: The PROBE (open-label) design did not have the advantages of a double-blind trial.
criticisms.quote: The IDEAL study was carried out with the PROBE design and, thus, did not have the advantages of a double-blind trial.

criticisms.text: Bias for some physician-initiated end points (eg, revascularization, hospitalization for unstable angina) cannot be excluded due to open-label design.
criticisms.quote: the possibility of bias for some of the physician-initiated end points, such as coronary revascularization and hospitalization for unstable angina, cannot be excluded.

criticisms.text: Follow-up was shorter than anticipated by the protocol (median 4.8 years vs anticipated 5.5 years to reach endpoints).
criticisms.quote: the follow-up duration was only a median of 4.8 years even though the study protocol anticipated the prespecified number of primary end points to be reached after a median of 5.5 years.

criticisms.text: Adherence was excellent but not as good in the atorvastatin group as in the simvastatin group.
criticisms.quote: although adherence with this therapy was excellent, it was not as good as in the simvastatin group.

criticisms.text: Reporting bias for nonserious adverse events leading to discontinuation is possible given the open-label design.
criticisms.quote: the possibility of reporting bias is present given the open-label design of the trial.
